q-44574.name: Question 1
q-44574.problem: Find the values of $k$ for which the quadratic equation $2{x}^{2}+4x+k=0$ has two distinct real solutions.
q-44574.worked_solution:
The equation has two distinct real solutions if its discriminant is positive. So, we need to find the values of $k$ so that the discriminant is positive.

First, we calculate the discriminant. We have $a=2,$ $b=4$ and $c=k,$ so the discriminant is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={b}^{2}-4ac \\  & =(4)^{2}-4(2)(k) \\  & =16-8k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the values of $k$ such that the discriminant is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & >0 \\ 16-8k & >0 \\ 16 & >8k \\ 8k & <16 \\ k & <2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the given equation will have two distinct real solutions if $k<2.$

q-83537.name: Question 2
q-83537.problem: Consider the equation $-{x}^{2}-2x+7=0.$ How many distinct real solutions does it have?
q-83537.worked_solution:
To quickly determine the number of solutions, we can compute the discriminant. We have $a=-1,$ $b=-2,$ and $c=7,$ so the discriminant is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={b}^{2}-4ac \\  & =(-2)^{2}-4(-1)(7) \\  & =4+28 \\  & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Since the discriminant is positive $(D>0),$ the equation has two distinct real solutions.

q-83540.name: Question 3
q-83540.problem: Consider the equation $-2{x}^{2}-8x-8=0.$ How many distinct real solutions does it have?
q-83540.worked_solution:
To quickly determine the number of solutions, we can compute the discriminant. We have $a=-2,$ $b=-8,$ and $c=-8,$ so the discriminant is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={b}^{2}-4ac \\  & =(-8)^{2}-4(-2)(-8) \\  & =64-64 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since the discriminant is zero $(D=0),$ the equation has one distinct real solution.
